name: Carmine Tsunami
iocPatterns: High volumes of disposable C2 domains
keyCapabilities: Cross-platform malware deployment (Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS)
Evidence removal and forensic footprint reduction
Cyberweapon sales via the REIGN platform
Command and Control (C2) through diverse infrastructures
Credential harvesting from system services (LSASS/iOS Keychain)
Automated management of child processes to evade detection
recommendedActions: Enable 'Lockdown Mode' on all iOS devices belonging to high-risk personnel.
Implement endpoint protection capable of identifying and blocking off-network credential access attempts (e.g., LSASS monitoring).
Deploy advanced email security solutions to identify and block hidden payloads in .lnk, .chm, and malicious PDF files.
Audit and restrict outbound traffic to known file-sharing platforms like MEGA for large data transfers.
Ensure all browsers and system components are patched against zero-day exploits targeting iMessage and other messaging protocols.
Segment high-value assets from general corporate networks to limit lateral movement possibilities.
Integrate specific forensic indicators of Tsunami and KingsPawn into EDR/SIEM watchlists.
Perform periodic audits of Office 365 environments for unauthorized account reconnaissance or configuration changes.
campaignsText: Carmine Tsunami operates primarily as a service-oriented threat actor, providing 'access as a service' to government clients. Their operational tempo is persistent, evidenced by the maintenance of extensive C2 infrastructure and the deployment of high-end malware across multiple platforms since at least 2022. They have been observed targeting diverse regions including the Middle East, Asia, and Europe, frequently focusing on civil society targets (journalists and NGOs) who may be of interest to their government clients.
description: Carmine Tsunami is a proficient private sector offensive actor (PSOA) and cyber mercenary linked to the Israeli-based firm QuaDream. The actor specializes in sophisticated mobile surveillance, zero-click exploits, and provide 'access as a service' via their REIGN platform, targeting high-value targets ranging from government officials to civil society members.
goals: The actor's primary objectives appear to be driven by financial gain through the sale of sophisticated cyber capabilities to governmental entities. Their targeting profile is dual-faceted: they provide tools for state-sponsored surveillance while simultaneously conducting operations against a broad spectrum of high-value targets, including those in the defense, telecommunications, and energy sectors. They specifically target individuals with access to sensitive information or who are influential in political and civil spheres, regardless of geographic borders.
